design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. Harold is standing at a pharmacy counter and says one thing: the chemist is holding his tablets, sort out whatever is stopping them, and let me pay and go home. Nothing in that names an approval, a denial, a reversal or an out-of-pocket total. The desk has to read the published rules and find that the counter price waits on two quite separate states of the record — an approved determination on a prior-authorisation tier, and an out-of-pocket total that agrees with the pharmacy record — discover from the file that neither holds, work out an approval term from six independent stretches of record, restate the accumulator from four more (including another product's card ledger), and only then price a ninety-day fill that straddles the deductible boundary. The difficulty is all in reading policy, reconciling ledgers and arithmetic: three writes, three tools, each named by exactly one policy, and every figure on a record the share finders return.

SCOPE. Occupied by task 0: pdp_ext_penalty_relief and pdp_ext_premium_arrears_settlement, with the tools post_penalty_removal_e1c246c8 and authorize_arrears_payment_7dfec3b3 — the premium and penalty side of the charter (subjects pdp_penalty_removal and pdp_premium_payment, base policies pdp_premium_posting, pdp_premium_billing, pdp_premium_delinquency and pdp_late_enrollment_penalty). This task claims the whole of the rest of its own tree and nothing task 0 touched: pdp_ext_counter_cost_share (pdp_pharmacy_claim_adjudication, settle_counter_fill_eaef344a), pdp_ext_troop_restatement (pdp_coverage_stage_update, restate_out_of_pocket_total_a40a5cef) and pdp_ext_exception_approval_term (pdp_coverage_determination_decision, issue_exception_decision_dd13544d), over the base policies pdp_point_of_sale_cost_share, pdp_coverage_stage_progression, pdp_transition_and_utilization_management and pdp_coverage_determination_timeliness. With task 1 closed the difficulty has M = 2 tasks and every extended policy is claimed exactly once, with no overlap in policies or tools. Deliberately left unclaimed in the charter, because two tasks cannot carry everything: pdp_enrollment_created, pdp_voluntary_disenrollment, pdp_application_withdrawal, pdp_redetermination_filing and the lifecycle transitions.

STEP 0 DRAW (paste of scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/tasks/part_d_pharmacy_and_coverage_desk --tasks 2):

  {"task": 1, "key": "env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/part_d_pharmacy_and_coverage_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 4]}
The tree therefore has exactly two prerequisite problems. Of the three drawn factor counts, 6 went to pdp_ext_counter_cost_share, 6 to pdp_ext_exception_approval_term and 4 to pdp_ext_troop_restatement; the multiset {4, 6, 6} matches the draw.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  Root problem: pdp_ext_counter_cost_share — the problem Harold's request points at ("what do I pay for these tablets").
  Prerequisite problems: pdp_ext_troop_restatement and pdp_ext_exception_approval_term. The shape is a fan-out: both hang off the root and neither depends on the other.
  Edge pdp_ext_counter_cost_share <- pdp_ext_troop_restatement.
    kind: value_input. gate: troop_on_record, a compute binding of the root policy. form: state, no fallback_reason: the out-of-pocket total standing on the enrollment is a field the enrollment record shows and the enrollment finder returns.
    Prerequisite sentence: "What the member pays at the counter is not fixed before the out-of-pocket total standing on the drug plan enrollment agrees with every fill the pharmacy record shows paid and every fill it shows backed out for the contract year."
    Four-point test. (1) It joins this policy's own result (what the member pays at the counter) to what it waits on with the ordering connective "before", in the negated direction. As the exact contrapositive it reads "the counter price is fixed only after the out-of-pocket total standing on the enrollment agrees with every fill the pharmacy record shows paid and every fill it shows backed out for the contract year": same result, same waited-on state, same quantifier scope over "every fill", nothing added, dropped or split. (2) Its XX side is a record-visible state — a total standing on the enrollment and agreeing with the fills the pharmacy record shows — named in the words the tables and finders use, with no action and no performer. (3) No tool, policy id, snake_case token or row id appears. (4) Its strength matches the edge's condition exactly: a hard "not fixed before", over the same closed set of fills.
    Direction: negated, because what waits here is a price being released to a member at a till, and a desk states a release in the negated voice ("we cannot fix what you pay until the record is straight") rather than as a charge being fixed. Task 0's settlement sentence runs in the affirmative direction for the opposite reason, so the difficulty's charter carries both.
    Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: pdp_enrollments.troop_accumulated is written by restate_out_of_pocket_total_a40a5cef alone; the other four tools write pdp_premium_ledger, pdp_coverage_determinations and pdp_pharmacy_claims.
    Derivation: the counter rule says the price waits on the enrollment's out-of-pocket total agreeing with the pharmacy record -> the enrollment carries 360.00 while the record carries five paid fills, two reversals, an out-of-network fill and a card that has met part of the spending -> the only rule whose result is a restated out-of-pocket total on the enrollment is the restatement rule -> restate, then price.
  Edge pdp_ext_counter_cost_share <- pdp_ext_exception_approval_term.
    kind: state_gate. gate: pdp_point_of_sale_cost_share.determination_on_record. form: state, no fallback_reason: an approved determination standing on the member's coverage determination record with its approved through date is exactly what that table holds.
    Prerequisite sentence: "What the member pays at the counter for a fill on a tier the plan enforces prior authorisation on is not fixed until an approved coverage determination for that product stands on the member's coverage determination record, good through a day not earlier than the fill date."
    Four-point test. (1) Ordering connective "not until", negated direction; its contrapositive reads "is fixed only once an approved coverage determination for that product stands on the record, good through a day not earlier than the fill date", with the same scope. (2) XX is a record-visible state: a determination standing on the record, its disposition and its approved through date. (3) No tool, id or code token. (4) Scope matched exactly to the condition, and narrowed to fills on a tier the plan enforces prior authorisation on, which is what base's own gate says.
    Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: pdp_coverage_determinations rows carrying a decision outcome of approved are written by issue_exception_decision_dd13544d alone.
    Derivation: the counter rule says a fill on a prior-authorisation tier waits on an approved determination good through a day not earlier than the fill date -> the held fill sits on the preferred brand tier, which this plan enforces prior authorisation on, and the record carries only a denial and a pending request -> the only rule whose result is an approval recorded on a request is the approval-term rule -> decide, then price.
    Neither sentence contains the other, and neither contains task 0's; each is located in the corpus by its own text.
    Seed evidence that each edge is false at the opening, the topological order, the commuting proof and the per-edge deletion sensitivity are all recorded in prerequisite_closure.
    Customer's own write: the root's target_tool settle_counter_fill_eaef344a is owner=user. Money leaves Harold's own card and only he may authorise it; the desk unlocks and hands it over at the root's place in the order, and the receipt it returns enters the shared transcript.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write 1, subject pdp_coverage_stage_update. Governing base policies: pdp_coverage_stage_progression and pdp_transition_and_utilization_management, both of which declare eligibility: [] in the blueprint, so both enter the contract as policy_scope with no evidence bindings. There is no approval, status, term or dedup gate hiding in their prose: the stage rule says in terms that "the stages are restated from the accumulator rather than kept as a separate fact", which is a licence to restate, not a gate on it.
  Write 2, subject pdp_coverage_determination_decision. Governing base policy: pdp_coverage_determination_timeliness, gate decision_within_deadline, kind time.
    Condition, verbatim: "The plan gives its decision no later than the decision deadline counted from the time the plan received the request, or from the time the prescriber's supporting statement arrived where the request is an exception." Starting business event: the time the plan received the request. Authoritative anchor: pdp_coverage_determinations.received_time. Direction: not_after. Duration: variants.coverage_determination_standard_hours, which is 72 for Ridgecrest RxSecure Value (PDP). Unit: elapsed_hours. Counting rule, verbatim: "Hours are counted as full 24-hour periods from the recorded receipt time, calendar days are counted from the day after the receipt date with every day of the week counting, a decision given exactly on the deadline is in time, and the two units are never mixed." Boundary: inclusive.
    Positive case at frozen_time: received 14:20 on 2026-09-20, deadline 14:20 on 2026-09-23, decision given 11:05 on 2026-09-21, about 20 hours and 45 minutes in — comfortably in time. Negative case: a request received at 14:20 on 2026-09-17 would have had its deadline at 14:20 on 2026-09-20 and a decision now would be out of time, so the request would already have gone to the independent review entity and the correct terminal state would be a different one. Both are recorded in solvability_contract.temporal_feasibility[0].boundary_check. The hours are full 24-hour periods measured from a recorded clock time, never calendar days, which is why the receipt time and not merely the receipt date is read.
  Write 3, subject pdp_pharmacy_claim_adjudication. Governing base policies: pdp_point_of_sale_cost_share and pdp_transition_and_utilization_management.
    coverage_in_force_on_fill_date (state): "The enrollment is in a status of active or premium_grace_period on the fill date of the prescription." Evidence: the enrollment stands active with coverage from 2026-01-01 and no coverage end date, and the fill date is the handling date. Correlation: pdp_enrollments.pdp_enrollment_id bound to the call's pdp_enrollment_id.
    determination_on_record (authorization): "Where the fill's formulary tier is one the tier enforces prior authorisation on, an approved coverage determination covering that product and still inside its approved through date is on record." The held fill is on tier_3_preferred_brand and Ridgecrest RxSecure Value (PDP) lists that tier among its prior_authorization_required_tiers, so the gate bites. Its correlation group is the pair pdp_pharmacy_claims.pdp_pharmacy_claim_id and pdp_coverage_determinations.pdp_determination_id, which is why the counter tool carries both as arguments; the second is bound to the approval recorded at step 11 through its real DB delta.
    pdp_transition_and_utilization_management declares eligibility: [] and enters as policy_scope.
  Overrides declared, none undeclared: 2 entries in all across this task's three policies. pdp_point_of_sale_cost_share's clause "What the member pays at the counter is taken from the negotiated price for the product" is superseded, because where the fill the pharmacy is holding carries no negotiated price this policy takes the cost share from a price standing on another of the member's fills. The ceiling itself is no longer overridden at all: the member never pays more than the plan's negotiated price recorded for the held fill, which is base's own rule, so that declaration was withdrawn. pdp_coverage_stage_progression's clause "Only what the member or a qualifying third party actually paid counts toward the threshold: plan payments, premiums and the late enrollment penalty never count" is superseded by a sentence that keeps every exclusion it states and adds two: never more than the plan's negotiated price recorded for the fill, and never what a supplemental benefit card met at a pharmacy. Every other base clause on these three subjects is inherited untouched, including the insulin cap, the vaccine rule, the out-of-network footing and the transition supply rules, none of which this task's world exercises.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD.
  Write 1 target object: the out-of-pocket accumulator of enrollment 7abdbf6e-f4bb-4679-9db1-91851ac8ca1c for contract year 2026. Correlation key: pdp_pharmacy_claims.pdp_enrollment_id. Rows included in the aggregates: the five rows with event_type pdp_pharmacy_claim_adjudication and claim_status paid, the two rows with event_type pdp_pharmacy_claim_reversal, and the out-of-network row read for its negotiated price. Rows excluded: the held fill of 2026-09-21, which is neither paid nor a reversal and contributes nothing until it is priced. The card's ledger is read on its own programme reference and is never written.
  Write 2 target object: the single open drug coverage request of 2026-09-20. Correlation key: pdp_coverage_determinations.source_determination_id on the new decision, which names that request and no other. Rows excluded: the request of 2026-04-10, which the denial of 2026-04-13 already disposed of, and the denial itself, which is read only as evidence of a standing denial.
  Write 3 target object: the held fill of 2026-09-21. Correlation key: pdp_pharmacy_claims.source_pharmacy_claim_id on the new priced fill, which names the held fill. Rows excluded: the out-of-network rejected fill of 2026-05-30, which is the other rejected row on the record and is distinguished by its rejection reason, its pharmacy standing and its fill date.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
  customers (1 row): the caller; his subsidy level of none is what keeps the tier's own figures in force rather than the low-income copays.
  pdp_enrollments (1 row): the holding. The plan held fixes the deductible of 615.00, the preferred brand figures of 44.00 and 51.00, the generic figure of 6.00, the retail and mail multipliers of 3.0 and 2.5 and the 72-hour decision deadline; status active selects the top tier of both the gathering and the reversal ladders; troop_accumulated 360.00 is the deliberately stale figure the restatement exists to correct, and the figure the whole value_input edge turns on.
  pdp_pharmacy_claims (9 rows). Five fills standing paid: their count of five drives four separate ladders (the gathering window, the out-of-network basis, the term counting basis and the deductible basis), their member payments are the 360.00 gathered, their prices give the 128.00 and 36.00 the two price ladders fall back on, and four of them being mail order is the whole of the channel allowance. Two reversals: they are the whole of the reversal factor, and their count of two is what puts it on its top tier; delete one and the factor falls to its three-month tier and the restated total moves. One out-of-network rejected fill: it is the whole of the out-of-network factor, and its negotiated price of 96.00 against the 145.00 the member handed over is what makes the two tiers of that factor give different numbers. The held fill: its tier, pharmacy standing, days supply and price are four of the six inputs of the counter price.
  NEAR-MISS ROWS. (a) The out-of-network rejected fill is the decoy for the held fill: both carry claim_status rejected, and a reader who takes the earlier one prices a 30-day tier_3 fill at an out-of-network pharmacy for 96.00 instead of a 90-day preferred-retail fill for 786.00. (b) The fill of 2026-06-15 falls three months and six days before the handling date, just outside the three-month window the gathering baseline uses. (c) The fill of 2026-02-18 falls seven months back, just outside the six-month window the gathering rule's middle tier uses, so a reader who takes that tier loses 34.00. (d) The denial of 2026-04-13 is a decision on the same product and the same tier as the open request; a reader looking for "the determination" may take it and find no approved through date. (e) The request of 2026-04-10 is the decoy open request; only the 2026-09-20 one is still pending.
  pdp_coverage_determinations (3 rows): the open request that earns the term, the standing denial that earns the review allowance, and the request that denial disposed of.
  advantage_enrollments (1 row): read-only background. The member holds Ridgecrest Advantage Elite Choice (PPO), the one Advantage tier whose part_d_included is false, which is exactly the case base's pdp_exclusivity_with_medicare_advantage allows to sit beside a stand-alone drug plan, and which is why a Healthy Options Card programme legitimately exists for him at all. Its premium balance is nothing and it carries no claims, so it lights no obligation in that difficulty; its own premium is withheld from Social Security.
  allowance_programs (1 row) and allowance_card_ledger (7 rows): the cross-difficulty evidence. The programme's active standing and its tier's own quarterly over-the-counter sublimit of 90.00 select the top tier of the card factor; the four settled pharmacy purchases totalling 168.00 are what put the member above that sublimit. Remove the purchases and the card factor falls to its middle tier and the restated total rises by 78.00. The three quarterly loads keep the card's balance of 62.50 honest against its own charter.
  No outcome stamp decides any factor: no row carries a "prior authorisation granted" or "counts toward out-of-pocket" flag. The enrollment's coverage_stage is read by no rule; the stage is restated from the accumulator, as base requires.
  Automatic-clause check: the enrollment is active with nothing owed, so no grace period, delinquency or termination clause is lit; there is no transition fill on the record, so the transition and refill-too-soon clauses are silent; the one open request is inside its deadline, so the automatic referral to the independent review entity is not due. The card programme is active and inside its benefit year, so no dormancy, expiry or forfeiture clause of that difficulty is lit.
  Cache design: troop_accumulated is a deliberate stale cache, declared here and in seed_consistency. It is the one row field that disagrees with the ledger at the opening, and correcting it is the whole of the first prerequisite. Harold's reaction to it is passive and uninformed: asked what he has spent this year he says he cannot say and keeps no slips.

PERSONA DESIGN. Harold is a retired bus mechanic in his late seventies, standing in the shop with his coat on, mildly cross with the telephone rather than with anybody in it; the voice is short, concrete and a little dry. Volunteered at the opening: the chemist is holding a prescription, he wants whatever is stopping it dealt with, he wants to pay today at this counter, and he will put it on his own card himself rather than have it put through for him. Given only when asked: his name, date of birth, Medicare identifier, telephone number, address, whether anyone acts for him, what he thinks the tablets cost (he did not take it in), what he has spent this year (he cannot say) and what is on the benefit card (no idea). Passive reactions woven into the narration: he will not argue about the amount once told; he makes the payment himself when it is handed over and reads the receipt back if asked; if a figure is quoted and nothing follows he asks whether he may pay it now; and he closes only when he hears the fill has gone through and the bag can be handed over. He never names a determination, a denial, a reversal or an out-of-pocket total, and he never corrects a wrong figure.

PRESENTED DIFFICULTY, DEPTH AND BREADTH. Depth: surface goal (pay for the held tablets) -> the counter rule's two prerequisite sentences -> the pharmacy record shows a fill rejected for prior authorisation on a tier this plan restricts, and an enrollment total that ignores two reversals, a card and an out-of-network fill -> the determination rules and the open request -> the approval term computation -> the stage rules and the card ledger -> the restatement -> only now are both waited-on states true -> the counter computation -> hand the payment over. Breadth: sixteen distinct record reads across four tables and two products, sixteen ladders over three computations, and two of the three computations reading stretches the other does not. Sixteen of the sixteen ladder tiers taken are non-fall-through.
  EASY MISTAKES AND HOW POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Pricing the held fill at the formulary tier's 44.00 without the standard-retail addition: excluded by the sentence about what the dispensing pharmacy's standing adds. Pricing it at the one-month figure of 51.00: excluded by the sentence about fills for more than thirty days' supply. Pricing it at the 139.00 cost share without the deductible: excluded by the stage-boundary sentence, which bites because fills stand paid at the deductible stage and 786.00 exceeds what is still to be met. Measuring the deductible against the 360.00 the enrollment carries: excluded by the prerequisite sentence, which says in terms that the price is not fixed before that total agrees with the record. Taking the out-of-network fill as the held one: excluded by its rejection reason and its fill date. Counting the 145.00 the member handed over at the out-of-network pharmacy: excluded by the sentence taking the largest plan negotiated price recorded on such a fill. Counting the card's 168.00 in full, or not at all: excluded by the sublimit sentence. Approving for the plain 365 days: excluded by four separate allowance sentences. Deciding the April request instead of the September one: excluded by the April one's disposition.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify Harold; read the enrollment (Value, active, deductible stage, out-of-pocket total 360.00); read the nine pharmacy rows and the three determination rows; read his medical plan and his benefit card programme and ledger. Restate the out-of-pocket total: gathered 360.00 (five paid fills, at least four, active), card met 90.00 (active, 168.00 settled at or above the 90.00 sublimit), reversals 162.00 (two reversals, active), out-of-network counted 96.00 (such a fill stands, five paid fills) -> 204.00. Approve the open request: maintenance term 365 (standard determination, statement received), counted 360 (five paid fills, statement received, whole thirty-day cycles), less 60 (standing denial, five fills), plus 30 (four mail-order fills), less 18 (anchored to the 2026-09-03 fill), less 45 (quantity limits, two preferred-brand fills standing paid) -> 267 days, above the floor of 30, good through 2027-06-15. Price the fill: formulary tier figure 44.00 (preferred brand) plus a standing addition of 7.00 (standard retail), giving a supply charge 132.00 plus a standing addition of 7.00, giving a cost share of 139.00 (90 days, retail multiplier 3.0), acting price 786.00 (held fill carries a price, five paid fills), deductible still to be met 411.00 (615.00 less 204.00), split at the boundary 411.00 + 66.32 -> 477.32, under the negotiated price of 786.00; hand the payment to Harold.

RULE / COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP. Forward: every binding of all three policies that reads the world, aggregates, chooses, caps or rounds carries a verbatim rule quotation in compute_basis — eighteen entries for the restatement, sixteen for the approval term and seventeen for the counter price. Sensitive-word cross-check: "in the three months up to the handling date" attaches to within_months=3, "in the six months" to within_months=6, "every fill standing paid on the record" to the unwindowed aggregate, "settled" and "pharmacy and over-the-counter" to the matching eq filters on the card ledger, "at least the number" to a >= comparison, "the largest ... recorded" to MAX, "the latest" to LATEST, "rounded down to a whole cycle" to int(x / n) * n, "never below nothing" to MX(0, ...), "never issues a run shorter than the plan's floor" to MX(floor, ...), "held to the ceiling" to MN, "rounded once to two decimal places" to RND(x, 2). Reverse: reading the three rules through, every load-bearing sentence is claimed by a binding — the three gathering sentences, the three card sentences, the three reversal sentences and the three out-of-network sentences on the restatement; the three term sentences, three counting sentences, three denial sentences, three channel sentences, three anchor sentences and three quantity sentences on the approval term; the three one-month sentences, three supply sentences, three price sentences, three deductible sentences, three split sentences and three ceiling sentences on the counter price. The ordering and rounding sentences are claimed by the result bindings. No sentence is unclaimed and no filter appears in an expression the quoted sentence does not state.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT ALONE. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this rationale masked, and working only from the rules as they will be published, the tool schemas, what the share finders return on this DB and Harold's actual lines, the re-derivation runs: he wants the held fill priced and paid, so the counter rule applies; that rule says the price is not fixed before the enrollment's out-of-pocket total agrees with the pharmacy record, and the record disagrees with it in three ways; it also says a fill on a prior-authorisation tier is not fixed until an approved determination stands on the record, and only a denial and a pending request stand there. Restate to 204.00; approve for 267 days; then the deductible still to be met is 411.00, the cost share 139.00, the acting price 786.00, the fill splits at the boundary and the member hands over 477.32 for coverage of the held fill. That matches gold in value, shape, moment and order, and the two prerequisites commute. The only place two readings seemed possible was which rejected fill is "the one the pharmacy is holding", and the rejection reason code plus the fill date settle it exclusively.

REVISION LOG.
  1. Symptom: the first draft put the benefit card's offset on the counter price as well as on the out-of-pocket restatement. Root cause: with the card meeting part of the counter payment, the new priced fill would record what the member handed over net of the card while the seeded past fills record the gross cost share, so the card's share would have been netted twice across the two computations. Change: the card was left in the restatement alone, where it excludes what the plan's own money met on past fills, and the counter price gained the acting-price and ceiling factors in its place. Re-run: the restatement still moves 90.00 and the counter price is unaffected by the card; no double count remains. Propagation: the counter policy's rule, factors, compute_basis and baseline were rewritten in the same pass, as was the cross_category block, which the counter policy now declares as [].
  2. Symptom: the counter tool needed two arguments it had no business reason for. Root cause: the blueprint fixes determination_on_record's correlation group as the pair pdp_pharmacy_claims.pdp_pharmacy_claim_id and pdp_coverage_determinations.pdp_determination_id, so the gate can only be bound through arguments of those names. Change: the tool takes the held fill's reference as pdp_pharmacy_claim_id, which it writes back as the source of the new priced fill, and the approval's reference as pdp_determination_id, which it writes as the determination reference; the second is resolved from the real DB delta of the approval step rather than invented. Re-run: the tool contract gate passes and the solvability gate's required and declared gates match exactly. Propagation: the tool docstring, the gold arguments, the tracing entries and the base-invariant card changed together.
  3. Symptom: the approval term's channel allowance did not bite, because only two of the seeded fills were dispensed by mail order against a threshold of three. Root cause: the world was laid out before the ladder's threshold was fixed. Change: the two earlier generic fills were moved to the mail order pharmacy, giving four. Re-run: the factor's sensitivity moved from equal-to-gold to 237. Propagation: the seed rows, the factor_trace line, the tracing entry and the seed-row section of this rationale were updated in the same pass.

REWORK ROUND 2 — SOURCE-LAYER AUDIT.
  T1-1 / F-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, closed by redesign). counter_price_ceiling was decoration on this world: it registered as weight-bearing only because its declared baseline was latest_paid_price, a figure the policy's own baseline.rule never selects, and under the baseline that rule does state — the held fill's negotiated price of 786.00 — the scored value was unchanged at 473.98. (The round-2 write-up justified striking it with the claim that 'a ceiling at p can never bind on any world'. user_scenario:
Harold Deakins spent thirty-one years under the bonnets of Marwick's buses and has never once enjoyed a telephone call to an insurance company. He is standing just inside the pharmacy on Ivyhurst Road at eleven in the morning, coat still on, because the girl behind the counter has told him she cannot hand over his new tablets and that he had better ring the plan himself. He is not angry with her. He is, faintly, angry with the telephone.

What he wants is simple and he says it in the first breath: the chemist is holding a prescription for him, he would like whatever is stopping it dealt with, and then he would like to pay for it and go home. He is quite clear that he wants to settle it today and at this counter rather than come back, and he is equally clear that he is not leaving until somebody tells him a number. He says he will put it on his own card himself when the time comes; he does not want anybody putting it through on his behalf without him seeing the figure first.

Asked who he is, he gives his name as Harold Deakins and his date of birth as 1948-11-02. If the number on the Medicare card is wanted he reads it out as 2KW9RT3HQ48, slowly, because he has to hold it at arm's length. His telephone number is 3127760453 and his address is 62 Ivyhurst Road, Marwick, if either is asked for. He is content for the agent to look at anything on his file and says as much without being asked twice. Nobody acts for him and there is nobody else with him.

He does not know what the tablets cost. If he is asked he says the pharmacist mentioned a figure once and he did not take it in, and that the agent had better read it off whatever they can see rather than go by him. He cannot say what he has spent on his prescriptions this year either; he pays what he is asked and keeps none of the slips. If he is asked about the card the plan sends him for the chemist and the groceries, he says he has it in his wallet and uses it for the odd bottle of paracetamol, and he has no idea what is left on it.

Once he is told what he has to hand over he does not argue about the amount, though he may mutter that it is a good deal more than the last lot. When the agent passes the payment over for him to make, he makes it, and if he is asked to confirm it afterwards he reads back what comes up on the receipt. If a figure is quoted to him and then nothing happens, he waits a beat and asks whether he can pay it now or whether he is meant to do something else.

When he hears that the fill has gone through and the pharmacist can hand the bag over, he says that is all he wanted, thanks the agent rather more warmly than he began, and puts the telephone away.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.member_paid_amount: Value: 477.32. The figure the formulary tier gives — the plan's 30-day preferred retail cost share for the tier the held fill sits on — is 44.00, because the fill is on the preferred brand tier. The supply charge the fill earns is 132.00, because the fill is for ninety days, more than thirty, and the pharmacy carries standard cost sharing, so that figure is multiplied by the plan's ninety-day retail multiplier of 3.0; the multiplier acts on the formulary tier's figure alone and never on what the pharmacy's standing adds. The pharmacy's standing adds 7.00, the difference between the tier's standard retail preferred brand figure of 51.00 and its preferred brand figure of 44.00, so the cost share for the fill is 139.00. The price the cost share is taken from is 786.00, because the held fill carries a negotiated price and the fills standing paid number five, at least the settled therapy count of three. The deductible still to be met is 411.00, because the fills standing paid number five, at least the long fill history of four, and the out-of-pocket total standing on the enrollment is 204.00, so the plan's annual deductible of 615.00 less 204.00 applies. Fills stand paid at the deductible stage and 786.00 is more than 411.00, so the fill is split at the boundary: the member pays the 411.00 still to be met together with the cost share in the proportion the price above the deductible bears to the whole price, 139.00 times 375.00 divided by 786.00, which is 66.32 after rounding, giving 477.32. The member never pays more than the plan's negotiated price recorded for the held fill, 786.00, and 477.32 is below it. Any agent who reads the held fill, the five fills standing paid and the restated out-of-pocket total converges on 477.32.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The root has two prerequisites that may be taken in either order. The out-of-pocket restatement writes only pdp_enrollments.troop_accumulated; the approval writes only a new pdp_coverage_determinations row whose reference number is a content hash of the enrollment, the member, the request it disposes of, the product and the term, none of which the restatement touches. Neither reads what the other writes. Replaying this task's gold in the declared order and again with the two unlock-and-call pairs swapped gives byte-identical terminal DB hashes: a19935eb3a69e6cbfa141fdf63a8b3c68607a1f3ff054cd90cb261716375d57f in both runs, and the scored counter price is 477.32 either way. Both orders are therefore one solution, not two.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the out-of-pocket restatement and replaying everything else leaves troop_on_record at the 360.00 the enrollment carries, so the deductible still to be met is 255.00 rather than 411.00 and the scored member_paid_amount moves from 477.32 to 348.90; the terminal enrollment also still carries 360.00 instead of 204.00.

Skipping the approval leaves the terminal coverage determination record without the approved decision row pdpdec_445fdde28c22 altogether, and the held fill is priced with a determination reference naming a determination that does not exist, so base's requirement that an approved determination stand on record for a fill on a prior-authorisation tier is unsatisfied at the moment of pricing. The terminal hash differs on the missing decision row and on the priced fill's own reference number, which is a content hash that includes the approval reference.
